## Themes

These rows serve four aims: a person can follow what they are told (`teach`, `i-have-adhd`, and the new `in-your-own-words` and `sharpen`), work picks up where it stopped (the new `recall`), claims of safety and of being finished carry proof (`review`, `test-driven-development`, and the new `figure-it-out` playbook, adopted whole), and a repeated mistake is fixed at the highest level that works (`authoring-for-agents`, `principle-type-system-discipline`, and the new `principle-no-comments` with its `no-comments` sweep). The new units follow the owner's rulings of 2026-11-05 and, for `recall`, 2026-11-06. Capabilities still with no home among ours are deferred to the owner's review of deferred and rejected traits (`cr-r2pa.3.3`), and any wording that follows goes through `cr-r2pa.3.4`. The recommendations are ruled as one set, with named exceptions. Adopts into a unit not built yet carry no frozen wording, so the critic of each new body, which `harness_lifecycle/playbook.md` requires, must map every such row, including its modification and the delivery wording in its reason, to delivered `file:line` evidence before completion; a deviation returns for a ruling, and the build brief cites the sealed report.

## skill:pstack/skills/no-comments

Compared with `none`; upstream tree hash `c6ebd67b8bef1885ff6052a1f6c740d3e8fb92a0d5137db1f1480eb95dcb3049`.

Suggested: interrogate · purpose match: none · flag: suggested differs
Purpose: Upstream runs a comment-deleting audit through a spawned role and acts on its findings. Ours has no comment audit; `review` reports findings on a change and removes nothing by itself. The owner's ruling of 2026-11-05 makes it a principle for the rules and a manual skill for the sweep, without the persona.
Reason: Compared with none: `review` only overlaps on handling findings, and nothing of ours audits comments. Suggested interrogate by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. default-review-scope: Work on whatever files or diff the caller supplied; failing that, compare the working tree and current changes with the base branch, which defaults to main. (SKILL.md:15)
2. dedicated-comment-critic-role: Spawn a fixed subagent role, named comment-sicko, to do the comment audit, and pass it the scope. (SKILL.md:9, SKILL.md:19)
3. defer-to-fresh-critic: Give weight to the critic's fresh perspective over the caller's own attachment. (SKILL.md:11)
4. no-restating-role-rules: Do not repeat the critic's rules in the spawn request. (SKILL.md:19)
5. per-subagent-reasoning-and-speed: Choose each subagent's reasoning level and speed tier for its job according to a shared guide. (SKILL.md:19)
6. inspect-report-and-diff: Check both the critic's report and its actual diff before accepting anything. (SKILL.md:20)
7. reject-application-code-edits: Refuse any change the critic made to application code. (SKILL.md:20)
8. reject-scope-escapes: Refuse critic work outside the given scope. (SKILL.md:20)
9. reject-exception-protected-deletions: Refuse deletions of comments protected by a stated exception. (SKILL.md:20)
10. reject-misstated-kill-reasons: Refuse a report whose reason for a mandatory deletion is wrong. (SKILL.md:20)
11. reject-guilt-flags-on-kept-code: Refuse flags that treat intentionally retained code as being at fault. (SKILL.md:20)
12. reshape-flags-stay-actionable: Keep flags asking to restructure surprising first-party code open, without bringing their comments back. (SKILL.md:20)
13. keep-requires-unchangeable-proof: Allow a comment to survive only with proof it concerns something the team cannot alter. (SKILL.md:20)
14. audit-missed-suppressions: Check the scope for lint and TypeScript suppression comments the critic overlooked. (SKILL.md:20)
15. safety-suppressions-must-be-killed: Treat suppressions that bear on correctness or safety as mandatory-removal findings. (SKILL.md:20)
16. restore-only-with-exact-exception: Bring back a deleted comment only when an exact exception and proof within scope exist. (SKILL.md:20)
17. investigate-thin-importance-comments: Before accepting a thinly justified kill or keep of a comment marked important or do-not-remove, investigate its symbol's behavior and history. (SKILL.md:20)
18. ambiguity-defaults-to-deletion: Leave an ambiguous kill deleted, and delete a keep that is refuted or stays ambiguous. (SKILL.md:20)
19. single-rerun-with-named-failure: After rejecting a report, revert it and rerun the critic once, stating what went wrong. (SKILL.md:20)
20. second-rejection-fails-run: If the second report is also rejected, report it as open and fail the whole skill. (SKILL.md:20)
21. direct-fix-for-trivial-flags: Resolve simple accepted flags at once through edits such as removing an unused path or parameter, or calling the genuine API. (SKILL.md:21)
22. one-design-sketch-for-accepted-set: When a fix needs a design, run one design pass over all accepted flags and nearby code, stopping at the sketch. (SKILL.md:21)
23. design-and-implementation-separated: Keep shaping with the design pass and leave implementation to the later step. (SKILL.md:21)
24. smallest-root-cause-fix: Implement the smallest in-scope fix that addresses the underlying cause. (SKILL.md:22)
25. remove-all-named-workarounds: Eliminate every workaround the findings name. (SKILL.md:22)
26. out-of-scope-cause-reported: If the true cause lies beyond scope, ship the minimal fix available inside it and list the remainder as open. (SKILL.md:22)
27. principles-never-widen-scope: Treat guiding principles as intent only, never permission to expand the boundary or fix other instances. (SKILL.md:22)
28. no-symptom-guards: Never add a guard that merely masks a symptom. (SKILL.md:22)
29. constraint-comment-recognition: Treat comments that forbid removal, forbid rewording or require consulting someone as a distinct class. (SKILL.md:23)
30. leave-unchangeable-constraint-keeps: Leave kept comments that concern things outside the team's control. (SKILL.md:23)
31. offer-cheapest-enforcement: For other constraint comments, propose the least costly enforcement available in scope, whether a type, runtime check, test or CI lint. (SKILL.md:23)
32. encoding-approval-gate: Wait for approval of the encoding in live use, and require advance approval from the caller when unattended or under evaluation. (SKILL.md:23)
33. encode-then-delete: When approved, add the enforcement and then remove the comment. (SKILL.md:23)
34. unencoded-constraint-deleted-and-reported: Without approval, delete the comment, report the constraint as open and sketch any out-of-scope work. (SKILL.md:23)
35. closing-report-fields: Report how many comments were deleted and restored, reruns, the design sketch, fixes, offered and completed encodings, constraints left unenforced and remaining open items. (SKILL.md:24)

## skill:pstack/skills/typescript-best-practices

Compared with `principle-type-system-discipline`; upstream tree hash `fb35e49d1b6a48fa42d81fff0e4e9834b8f98e0ebcf188203680f1f4265df690`.

| Holder | Overlap | Placement match |
|---|---|---|
| principle-boundary-discipline | 2 |  |
| principle-model-the-domain | 1 |  |
| principle-sequence-verifiable-units | 0 | yes |
| principle-type-system-discipline | 4 |  |
| test-driven-development | 0 | yes |

Suggested: principle-type-system-discipline · purpose match: principle-type-system-discipline · flag: none
Purpose: Upstream is a TypeScript rule table with a pattern reference. Ours is the language-neutral principle those rules start from; `.repo-context/coding-style.md` is the language-specific document, for Python.
Reason: Compared with principle-type-system-discipline: upstream itself opens by applying that principle, and only a skill can be compared.

### Blind extraction

1. literal-discriminant-unions: Represent variants as a union tagged by a literal field so contradictory states cannot be written. (SKILL.md:14, references/patterns.md:30-41)
2. no-optional-field-bags: Do not model variant state with booleans plus optional fields. (SKILL.md:14, references/patterns.md:33-34)
3. one-discriminant-name: Settle on a single tag field name and use it consistently. (references/patterns.md:43)
4. branded-primitives: Intersect primitives with a readonly brand property so distinct identifiers cannot be swapped. (SKILL.md:15, references/patterns.md:7-10)
5. reuse-existing-brand-shape: Follow the established brand property shape and invent no other convention. (references/patterns.md:26)
6. brand-only-through-verifying-guard: Obtain a brand only from a type guard that truly checks the value, never from a cast. (SKILL.md:15, references/patterns.md:12-14)
7. validate-brand-once-then-trust: Check the brand at the boundary and let downstream code accept the type without re-checking. (SKILL.md:15, references/patterns.md:7, references/patterns.md:21-23)
8. constructive-illegal-state-removal: Compose the type only from legal pieces in place of runtime guards or hoped-for refinement types. (SKILL.md:16, references/patterns.md:47)
9. nonempty-variadic-tuple: Express a non-empty list as a tuple of one element plus a rest element. (SKILL.md:16, references/patterns.md:49-63)
10. single-narrowing-guard-for-plain-arrays: Where an ordinary array arrives, narrow it once with a guard so the fact travels in the type. (references/patterns.md:66-70)
11. even-length-as-pairs: Express an even-length list as an array of two-element tuples. (SKILL.md:16, references/patterns.md:72-76)
12. range-as-start-plus-duration: Express a time range as a start and a duration so a negative range cannot be written. (SKILL.md:16, references/patterns.md:78-86)
13. brand-only-on-real-confusion-risk: Leave a number unbranded unless a raw number could actually be passed in its place. (references/patterns.md:88)
14. derive-readings-over-representation: Expose other views of the data through helpers or derivations on top of the chosen representation. (references/patterns.md:88)
15. keep-loose-type-while-total: Stay with a plain array as long as every operation on it is defined for all inputs. (SKILL.md:17, references/patterns.md:92-96)
16. strengthen-on-lie-tells: Tighten the input type only where a non-null assertion, cast or impossible-case throw appears. (SKILL.md:17, references/patterns.md:98-110)
17. weaken-result-as-alternative: Return a possibly undefined result as the other way of making the signature total. (references/patterns.md:112)
18. external-data-is-unknown: Type all outside data as unknown and never as any. (SKILL.md:18, references/patterns.md:116-122)
19. narrow-before-use: Narrow unknown values before accessing them so the compiler checks the access. (references/patterns.md:116, references/patterns.md:124-129)
20. external-source-enumeration: Count RPC payloads, parsed JSON, posted messages, IPC, file contents, environment variables and database results as external. (references/patterns.md:132)
21. check-for-schema-library-first: Before hand-writing a field-by-field guard, find out which runtime schema library the repository uses and which schemas already exist. (SKILL.md:19, references/patterns.md:136)
22. schema-owns-validation-and-type: Have one schema own validation and infer the static type from it. (SKILL.md:19, references/patterns.md:136-151)
23. no-drifting-triplicate: Do not maintain a schema, a parallel interface and a guard that can disagree. (references/patterns.md:136)
24. safe-parse-for-expected-failure: Use the non-throwing parse variant when failure is an ordinary branch. (references/patterns.md:153)
25. use-repo-schema-helper-equivalent: Use the matching inference helper when the repository has a different schema library. (references/patterns.md:153)
26. no-new-schema-dependency-for-one-guard: Do not add a schema dependency for the sake of a single guard. (references/patterns.md:153)
27. no-as-casts: Disallow type assertions except after validation has established the claim. (SKILL.md:20, references/patterns.md:157)
28. no-partial-property-guard: Reject a guard that checks only some fields while claiming the full type. (references/patterns.md:165-168)
29. annotate-validator-with-proved-type: When the type is written first, annotate the validator with it so the compiler rejects a validator proving less. (references/patterns.md:179-185)
30. diagnose-cast-before-removing: When removing a cast, first find out why inference falls short. (references/patterns.md:187)
31. cast-fix-add-discriminant: If a discriminant is missing, add it and move to a tagged union. (references/patterns.md:189)
32. cast-fix-narrow-wide-source: If the source type is too broad, narrow it. (references/patterns.md:190)
33. cast-fix-parse-untyped-boundary: At an untyped boundary, parse using the schema responsible for that shape, adding one only where none exists. (references/patterns.md:191)
34. cast-fix-brand-or-satisfies: If the type truly cannot be expressed, use a brand or the satisfies operator. (references/patterns.md:192)
35. narrowing-preference-order: Prefer discriminant checks, then the in operator, then typeof or instanceof, then a user-defined guard, with a cast last and only after validation. (SKILL.md:21, references/patterns.md:196-209)
36. guards-must-verify: Require a type guard to really prove what it asserts, treating a false guard as worse than a cast. (SKILL.md:22, references/patterns.md:213-219)
37. guard-naming-convention: Name guards with an is or has prefix. (SKILL.md:22)
38. prefer-discriminant-over-guard: Use discriminant narrowing instead of a guard when it is available. (references/patterns.md:221)
39. never-assignment-exhaustiveness: In a switch's default arm, assign the switched value to a local typed never so a new variant becomes a compile error. (SKILL.md:23, references/patterns.md:225-257)
40. exhaustiveness-arm-by-switch-kind: Return the never value in value-producing switches and void it in statement switches. (references/patterns.md:235-238, references/patterns.md:251-254, references/patterns.md:259)
41. satisfies-over-as: Use the satisfies operator to check a value against a type while keeping its literal types. (SKILL.md:24, references/patterns.md:263-272)
42. parse-at-boundary-into-domain-type: Parse data at its point of entry into a named domain type. (SKILL.md:25, references/patterns.md:276)
43. loose-record-stops-at-parse: Allow a string-keyed unknown record, under any alias, to exist only up to that parse. (SKILL.md:25)
44. trust-types-inside-no-revalidation: Rely on the types past the boundary and do not validate again deep in call chains. (SKILL.md:25, references/patterns.md:276, references/patterns.md:280)
45. wire-parse-ignores-unknown-fields: Parse wire formats with unknown fields ignored so forward-compatible changes do not break old clients. (references/patterns.md:278)
46. persisted-json-versioned: Store persisted JSON as a versioned blob. (references/patterns.md:279)
47. persisted-json-guarded-parse: Surround the parse of persisted JSON with try/catch. (references/patterns.md:279)
48. derive-from-generated-schema-types: When a proto, OpenAPI, GraphQL or migration definition already gives a shape, use its generated types and do not duplicate them. (references/patterns.md:284-301)
49. type-utilities-before-new-interface: Try Pick, Omit, Parameters, ReturnType, Awaited and typeof before declaring a new interface. (SKILL.md:26, references/patterns.md:303)
50. object-arguments: Pass a single object in place of positional arguments so order is irrelevant and calls read clearly. (SKILL.md:27, references/patterns.md:307-326)
51. hot-path-positional-exception: Skip object arguments on per-frame rendering, tokenizers, parsers and other tight loops where allocation matters. (SKILL.md:27, references/patterns.md:328)
52. no-mocking-what-can-run: Avoid mocks for anything that can be run, and mock only what cannot run locally. (SKILL.md:28)
53. real-test-primitives-with-leak-checks: Prefer the framework's real test primitives along with leak and disposable checks. (SKILL.md:28)
54. verify-ui-in-running-build: Confirm UI behavior in an actual running build. (SKILL.md:28)
55. structured-logger-with-debug-context: Emit diagnostics through a structured logger carrying sufficient detail to trace a problem starting from an id. (SKILL.md:29)
56. no-console-log-in-shipped-code: Forbid console.log in code that ships. (SKILL.md:29)

Purpose: Upstream changes a repository so a repeated agent mistake cannot recur. `authoring-for-agents` has the part on choosing a check before a prose rule, and AGENTS.md has the recurring-lesson rule. Neither audits a repository for repeated mistakes.
Reason: Compared with authoring-for-agents: the holder of the check-over-prose rules, and where the fix ladder would land. Suggested codebase-design by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. repo-change-over-reminder: Answer repeated corrections by altering the repository so the next agent cannot make the mistake. (SKILL.md:9)
2. worst-case-contributor-model: Assume each contributor is an agent limited to the files it opened, imitating the closest example and choosing the quickest route to a successful compile. (SKILL.md:11)
3. locally-right-is-globally-right: Arrange the repository so a change that looks correct from one file is correct everywhere. (SKILL.md:11)
4. mine-mistake-evidence: Collect mistakes from recent history, reverts, review remarks, agent instruction files and comments explaining workarounds. (SKILL.md:15)
5. group-into-mistake-classes: Cluster the found mistakes into classes. (SKILL.md:15)
6. two-occurrence-threshold: Count a class only after it has happened at least twice. (SKILL.md:15)
7. highest-level-fix-ladder: Try fixes in order of architecture, types, lint or CI, tests and finally docs, stopping at the highest level that works. (SKILL.md:17-22)
8. single-owner-for-state: Give each piece of state exactly one owner. (SKILL.md:19)
9. one-supported-way-per-task: Allow one sanctioned way of doing each task. (SKILL.md:19)
10. hide-internals-so-wrong-import-fails: Encapsulate internals so an incorrect import does not work. (SKILL.md:19)
11. single-source-for-synced-lists: Replace lists kept in sync by hand with one source of truth. (SKILL.md:19)
12. delete-copyable-old-ways: Remove outdated approaches and dead code an agent might imitate. (SKILL.md:19)
13. unwritable-bad-state-types: Use types so the wrong state cannot be expressed. (SKILL.md:20)
14. check-error-names-the-replacement: Where wrong code can still compile, add a CI check or lint rule whose message points at the specific file, type or function to use. (SKILL.md:20)
15. ratchet-on-common-patterns: When a pattern is already widespread, fail only on changes that add more of it. (SKILL.md:20)
16. fix-or-delete-insensitive-tests: Repair or remove a test that stays green when its behavior breaks. (SKILL.md:21)
17. fix-or-delete-implementation-coupled-tests: Repair or remove a test that goes red when only internals change. (SKILL.md:21)
18. docs-last-judgment-only: Reserve docs and agent rules for judgment calls as the final option, since skipping them makes nothing fail. (SKILL.md:22)
19. most-frequent-classes-first: Fix the classes that occur most often in this pass. (SKILL.md:26)
20. one-commit-per-class: Land each class's fix in its own commit. (SKILL.md:26)
21. prove-check-on-real-past-mistake: Show each new check failing against a mistake that actually occurred. (SKILL.md:26)
22. same-command-local-and-ci: Run the identical command on a developer machine and in CI. (SKILL.md:26)
23. inline-exception-with-reason: Record an exception on the offending line along with its justification. (SKILL.md:26)
24. expiring-exceptions: Give every exception an expiry date. (SKILL.md:26)
25. human-approved-exceptions: Require a person's approval for each exception. (SKILL.md:26)
26. rule-to-enforcer-table: Maintain in the agent instruction file a table pairing each rule with what enforces it. (SKILL.md:30)
27. correction-adds-rule: On each operator correction, fix the mistake and also add the rule. (SKILL.md:30)
28. unenforced-repeat-escalation: If a corrected rule already existed without enforcement, count it as a repeat and solve it at the top workable level within that change. (SKILL.md:30)
29. retire-impossible-rules: Remove a rule once its mistake can no longer occur. (SKILL.md:30)
30. report-class-evidence-level-rationale: Report for every class the supporting evidence, the chosen level and why no higher level worked. (SKILL.md:32)

## skill:pstack/skills/tdd

Suggested: test-driven-development · purpose match: test-driven-development · flag: none
Purpose: Upstream proves a bug fix with a test that fails first, and says when to add none. Ours covers the same cycle with more modes.
Reason: Compared with test-driven-development: the same job and the most overlap.

### Blind extraction

1. executable-bug-before-code-change: When a bug has a clear and cheap test path, make the failure runnable before touching production code. (SKILL.md:9)
2. fails-before-passes-after-goal: Aim for one focused regression test that is red before the fix and green after. (SKILL.md:9)
3. impracticality-skip-conditions: Add no new test when it would demand wide harness setup, fragile mocks, slow full-stack infrastructure, state only production has, unclear reproduction or heavy unrelated fixture changes. (SKILL.md:11)
4. bug-understanding-checklist: Identify intended behavior, current behavior, the affected path and the smallest observable reproduction. (SKILL.md:15)
5. narrowest-existing-check-type: Prefer the closest kind of test already used for that codepath. (SKILL.md:16)
6. no-from-scratch-test-path: Do not build a test path from nothing merely to follow the workflow. (SKILL.md:16)
7. test-first-smallest-catching-test: Write first the smallest focused test able to catch this bug. (SKILL.md:17)
8. encode-intent-not-implementation: Have the test express intended behavior, not mirror how the code works today. (SKILL.md:17)
9. confirm-failure-for-right-reason: Run the new test before fixing and, if it passes or fails for another reason, correct the test or reproduction first. (SKILL.md:18)
10. minimal-contract-preserving-fix: Make the smallest production change that gives the intended behavior and preserves neighboring contracts. (SKILL.md:19)
11. rerun-to-confirm-pass: Run the regression test again after the fix and confirm it is green. (SKILL.md:20)
12. closest-executable-fallback-check: When a failing test is impractical, substitute a targeted script, repro command, browser automation, snapshot diff, log assertion or narrow integration check. (SKILL.md:24)
13. no-test-over-bad-test: Prefer adding nothing to a test that mostly exercises mocks, encodes internals, depends on timing or global state, requires costly infrastructure for minor fixes, or would be discarded right after. (SKILL.md:26)
14. no-tests-bent-to-wrong-code: Do not alter tests only so they agree with incorrect behavior. (SKILL.md:30)
15. no-weakened-assertions: Keep existing assertions as strong unless expected behavior truly changed for a clear reason. (SKILL.md:31)
16. focused-regression-no-churn: Keep the regression test on the bug without broad fixture changes or added unrelated coverage. (SKILL.md:32)
17. flaky-bug-determinism: For a flaky bug, remove nondeterminism from the test as far as possible and document which signal it pins. (SKILL.md:33)
18. focused-first-then-sibling-coverage: When a bug reveals a wider failure class, land the focused regression first and only then consider related coverage. (SKILL.md:34)
19. report-failing-before-evidence: Name the check that failed before the fix and the failure it gave. (SKILL.md:40)
20. report-passing-after-evidence: Name the passing run after the fix and any nearby validation done. (SKILL.md:41)
21. explain-missing-red-evidence: If a red result before the fix could not be shown, say why and describe the substitute check. (SKILL.md:42)

Purpose: Upstream designs a phased workflow when no playbook fits, then runs it. No unit of ours does both: `planning` writes a plan and stops, `autonomous-run` and `decision-trail` run and log, and `wayfinder` settles decisions across sessions. The owner's ruling of 2026-11-05 makes it a new playbook, which steps call those units from.
Reason: Compared with decision-trail, the unit its Trail step calls and the computed pick; nothing of ours has its purpose, and a playbook cannot be compared. Suggested decision-trail by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. design-playbook-before-code: When no existing playbook fits, produce a phased workflow as the first deliverable, ahead of any code. (SKILL.md:9)
2. todolist-with-principles-first: Open a todo list whose first item is reading a principles section, then add each phase as an item. (SKILL.md:13)
3. ground-before-commit: Do the grounding before starting, and do not begin the run until the framing can be stated. (SKILL.md:17)
4. falsifiable-done-predicate: Define done as a claim that can be shown false. (SKILL.md:19)
5. quantified-scope-with-blockers: State scope in rough units and effort along with blockers grounding turned up. (SKILL.md:20)
6. rigor-scaled-to-reversibility: Pick a rigor level biased high, raised for one-way doors and wide impact and lowered for reversible low-stakes steps. (SKILL.md:21)
7. rigor-means-gates-and-artifacts: Define rigor as concrete gates and artifacts, not extra effort. (SKILL.md:21)
8. present-framing-and-tradeoffs: Show the human the framing and its tradeoffs ahead of a long run. (SKILL.md:23)
9. reversible-work-proceeds: Continue reversible work without waiting on the human. (SKILL.md:23)
10. single-checkpoint-on-long-run: Give a multi-hour run one checkpoint with the human. (SKILL.md:23)
11. atomic-landable-units: Split the work into atomic units that can each land independently. (SKILL.md:27)
12. riskiest-unknown-first: Order the units so the largest unknown is tackled first. (SKILL.md:27)
13. scaffold-and-verification-before-features: Put scaffolding and verification ahead of feature work. (SKILL.md:27)
14. harness-with-pre-change-baseline: Build the verification harness first and capture a baseline before changing anything, so results read as old against new. (SKILL.md:29)
15. design-contest-for-one-way-doors: For design choices that cannot be undone, run a design skill that pits alternatives against each other. (SKILL.md:30)
16. skip-design-contest-on-settled-work: Skip that design contest for mechanical work of known shape, and do not repeat it on a settled design. (SKILL.md:30)
17. fan-out-across-seams-only: Decide what runs in parallel, parallelizing only where the work has seams and not over-fanning. (SKILL.md:31)
18. worktree-per-worker: Give each parallel worker its own worktree or branch. (SKILL.md:31)
19. per-subagent-reasoning-and-speed: Choose each subagent's reasoning level and speed tier for its job according to a shared guide. (SKILL.md:31)
20. written-phase-list-for-review: Write down the designed phases as the thing the human reviews. (SKILL.md:32)
21. design-steps-into-todolist: Insert the designed steps as concrete todo items between the loop and audit entries. (SKILL.md:34)
22. rolling-log-rows: Add a trail row as each step lands, not all at the end. (SKILL.md:34)
23. hypothesis-per-unit: Treat each unit as an experiment with a stated hypothesis. (SKILL.md:38)
24. smallest-change-per-experiment: Make the smallest change that tests the hypothesis. (SKILL.md:38)
25. measure-against-predicate-on-artifact: Measure each change against the done predicate using the real artifact. (SKILL.md:38)
26. keep-or-revert-rule: Keep a change that moved things forward and revert one that did not. (SKILL.md:38)
27. verify-unit-before-next: Verify each unit before starting another instead of batching checks for the end. (SKILL.md:38)
28. artifact-inspection-over-self-report: Verify by looking at the artifact and never by accepting a self-report. (SKILL.md:40)
29. too-easy-pass-suspicion: When something passes too easily, question the observation method before crediting the system. (SKILL.md:40)
30. judge-paired-with-delegation: Pair delegated work with a judge. (SKILL.md:41)
31. reset-and-harden-on-gate-gaming: When a worker games the gate, reset it and strengthen the contract. (SKILL.md:41)
32. fix-wrong-gate-separately: When the gate itself is wrong, correct it in its own change and do not route around it. (SKILL.md:41)
33. three-value-verdict: Report results as verified, not verified or inconclusive, with inconclusive never counting as a pass. (SKILL.md:42)
34. no-hidden-negatives: Do not conceal negative results. (SKILL.md:42)
35. commit-the-trail: For ambitious work, commit the trail so it is visible to the reviewer within the pull request. (SKILL.md:46)
36. whole-result-on-real-product: Check the finished whole against the opening predicate on the real product, beyond the harness. (SKILL.md:50)
37. encode-recurring-corrections: Turn any recurring correction into a gate, lint rule, check or script. (SKILL.md:50)
38. closing-reply-fields: Reply with the designed playbook, rigor level and reason, trail path, what is verified against the predicate and what is open. (SKILL.md:52)

## skill:pstack/skills/blast-radius

Compared with `review`; upstream tree hash `83927611fb04217ba6855e2bf40f9401de4819031f18f331426e72312e2aa562`.

| Holder | Overlap | Placement match |
|---|---|---|
| doc:.repo-context/coding-style.md | 1 |  |
| doc:AGENTS.md | 2 |  |
| interrogate | 0 | yes |
| review | 0 | yes |
| systematic-debugging | 1 |  |

Suggested: systematic-debugging · purpose match: review · flag: suggested differs
Purpose: Upstream finds what a change breaks elsewhere and proves the one fact it is safe because of. `review` is where a person asking this now lands; `interrogate` proves findings by a run but attacks a change with adversaries and is not a one-agent check of safety.
Reason: Compared with review: the unit that holds checking a change, with a new branch reference for this question. `interrogate` shares the run-as-proof idea, not the deliverable. Suggested systematic-debugging by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. beyond-the-callers-focus: Spend the effort on breakage text search cannot reveal, not on listing callers. (SKILL.md:13)
2. distrust-plausible-writeup: Treat a convincing writeup as worthless by itself, because it reads the same whether or not it is true. (SKILL.md:17)
3. evidence-ladder-per-safety-fact: Grade each safety-bearing fact as asserted, cited to a line, failure walked through, executed in a script or test, or reproduced in the running app. (SKILL.md:21-27)
4. push-as-far-as-cheap-and-disclose: Take each fact as far up that ladder as is cheap and state where it stopped. (SKILL.md:21)
5. small-real-library-script: Normally reach the executed level with one short script that imports the library shipped with the app and invokes precisely the function at issue. (SKILL.md:29)
6. failing-loud-proof: Make the script or test fail noisily if the claim is wrong. (SKILL.md:26)
7. read-whole-change-including-unstated: Go through the diff, the symbols added, changed and deleted, and the behavior change the diff does not spell out. (SKILL.md:33)
8. pull-pr-and-commit-history: Retrieve the related PR and commits while reading the change. (SKILL.md:33)
9. single-safety-fact-search: Find the one fact that makes the change safe and clears most risky cases, and spend the time there, not on a long list of possibilities. (SKILL.md:34)
10. read-dependency-source-and-pin: Read the called library's source and confirm its pinned version and whether it is locally patched. (SKILL.md:35)
11. timing-and-lifecycle-analysis: Work out when things execute, including microtasks, unmount and teardown, and framework differences. (SKILL.md:35)
12. non-symbol-coupling-trace: Follow links symbol search misses: API JSON, database columns, wire formats, another language reading the same bytes, feature flags and code several hops away. (SKILL.md:35)
13. likelihood-and-cost-per-risk: Give each risk an honest probability and an honest cost. (SKILL.md:36)
14. confirmed-and-cleared-split: Keep confirmed risks apart from those checked and cleared. (SKILL.md:36)
15. real-line-citations: Cite actual file and line locations. (SKILL.md:36)
16. empty-search-is-an-answer: Count a search that finds nothing as a result. (SKILL.md:36)
17. no-invented-callers-or-apis: Never fabricate a caller or an API. (SKILL.md:36)
18. run-and-paste-proof: Write a script or test against the real code, run it and include what happened. (SKILL.md:37)
19. multi-model-review-for-wide-changes: For a big or wide change, put the same question to more than one model and merge the answers. (SKILL.md:38)
20. handback-what-it-does: Say what changed, including the non-obvious part. (SKILL.md:42)
21. handback-safety-fact-with-grade: State the safety fact, its ladder level and its proof, or mark it unproven. (SKILL.md:43, SKILL.md:50)
22. handback-risk-fields: For each risk give how it breaks, file and line, likelihood and severity, how to check it, and the proof for those that matter. (SKILL.md:44)
23. handback-cleared-list: List what was checked and why it is fine. (SKILL.md:45)
24. handback-pre-merge-check: Give the cheapest test or reproduction able to expose the actual bug, along with any script written. (SKILL.md:46)
25. strip-private-before-public: Remove private material before the writeup goes anywhere public. (SKILL.md:48)
